amendments.rule: A construct noun cannot take the article, so a pointed `בַּ` before one is preposition-only and the English *the* is supplied. Follow MACULA's morphology rather than the pointing. Where the chain's *nomen rectum* does carry an article, that morpheme takes the *the* the ASV writes for the chain even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously — `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone*, `כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל` → *the furnace of iron*. Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present, or for a second English *the* in a multi-level chain, which the article's own leaves for the outer construct: `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men*. **Fronting is what the anarthrous rendering forces, not a preference for the phrase's left edge.** Where the ASV instead renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before the construct and another before the rectum — `מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי` → *the families of the Kohathites*, `בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי` → *the sons of the Kohathites*, `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city*, `מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי` → *the families of the Levites* — nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one, exactly as an outer construct does in a multi-level chain. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as rule 47 reads which word its single *the* stands before. **And a rectum the ASV renders indefinitely is not an anarthrous one.** Where the article morpheme stands on the rectum, the ASV writes an indefinite article before the rectum's own word, and the phrase's single *the* stands before the construct — `נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם` → *the body of a man* — nothing is fronted: the *a* is that noun's own under rule 15, one word is not determined twice, and the article is `unrepresented` under this rule's last sentence while the construct takes a supplied *the*. What forces fronting is a rectum the ASV leaves with no determiner at all, as `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone* is, so read which determiner stands before the rectum's word before counting the phrase's *the*s. **A construct relation the ASV recasts as an English possessive is not a fronting either.** Where the ASV writes the rectum as a possessive standing before its head noun — `מִלַּת מַלְכָּא` → *the king's matter*, `שַׁלִּיטָא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the king's captain*, `שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ` → *the king's gate* — the *the* at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's own word, because an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor and not of the head noun. So the article on the rectum takes it and the construct noun keeps only its own word, a present article morpheme taking its English before a supplied one does; supply a *the* on the construct only where the ASV writes a second one, as `רַב טַבָּחַיָּא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the captain of the king's guard* does. Do not read the left edge as evidence of fronting: what fronting answers to is an anarthrous rectum, and here the rectum is the very word the *the* determines. **Read that as the determiner of the possessive, not as the word *the*, and read it whether or not the possessor carries an article of its own.** An English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor whatever that determiner is, so an indefinite *a* standing at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's word exactly as a *the* does, and where the possessor's word carries no article morpheme the determiner the ASV supplies still goes to that word rather than to the construct noun: `נְשִׂיא בֵית־אָב` → *a prince of* ***a fathers*** *house* gives *a fathers* to `אָב` and *of ... house* to `בַּיִת`, discontinuous around the possessive under rule 25. This is rule 15's supplied determiner placed by this rule's own reasoning — the noun that licenses an English *a* in such a phrase is the possessor, since *a father's house* is the house of *a* father — and the construct noun takes a determiner of its own only where the ASV writes a second one, on the terms just given. A `דִּי` or other relational morpheme standing between the two nouns is rendered inside the possessive and shares the rectum's unit under rule 30. **And a chain the ASV renders attributively under rule 28 places its supplied determiner on these same terms.** Where the ASV writes the construct noun as an attributive standing before the rectum's own word — `קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו` → *the tall cedars thereof*, `מִבְחוֹר בְּרֹשָׁיו` → *the choice fir trees thereof*, `יְרַק דֶּשֶׁא` → *the green herb*, `בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִיּוֹן` → *The virgin daughter of Zion* — and no article morpheme stands in the phrase, the single written *the* stands before the construct noun's word and that noun takes it as a supplied one, exactly as it does where the same chain is written with *of*. Do not hand it to the rectum on the ground that the rectum is the head noun of the English phrase: rule 15's direction to read the noun of the expression rather than its leftmost word governs a numeral and the noun it counts, where the numeral is not a noun the ASV determines at all, and it does not reach a construct chain, whose determiners this rule counts. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as above: where the ASV writes one for each, each noun takes the one standing before its own word, and where an article morpheme stands on the rectum the fronting sentences above govern as before. The unit still heads on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31, so `קוֹמַת` → *the tall* heads on *tall*. **And the same holds where the ASV renders the rectum attributively instead and the construct noun is the English head.** Where the rectum's word stands first and the construct's word after it — `דְּבַר עֶצֶב` → *a grievous word*, `אִישׁ חֵמָה` → *A wrathful man*, `מַחְשְׁבוֹת רָע` → *Evil devices* — and no article morpheme stands in the phrase, the single supplied determiner is still the construct noun's, because what this rule supplies is a determiner on the construct noun and not on whichever of the two words the ASV has put first. Do not hand it to the rectum on the ground that it stands before the rectum's word: the counting sentences above weigh the ASV's written determiners against the article morphemes standing in the phrase, and where no article morpheme stands there at all there is nothing to count, so the preceding paragraph's reasoning governs in either English order. Where the ASV writes a determiner for each word, each noun takes the one standing before its own word, as above. Read MACULA's morphology before applying any of this, since rule 15's direction to take the noun of the expression governs a noun with an absolute modifier standing beside it — `לֵב שָׂמֵחַ` → *A glad heart*, `שׁוֹר אָבוּס` → *a stalled ox* — where no construct relation is written and this rule's count does not arise. **A rectum that is a proper name is not an exception.** An article MACULA segments off a toponym takes the ASV's *the* on the same terms as one on a common noun, and is never set aside as lexicalized in the name: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* give the single written *the* to the article and leave the construct noun bare. **But an article the ASV spells into its name is already rendered.** Where the rectum is transliterated with its article — `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* — the article shares the name's unit under rule 30, it has taken its *the* inside that English word rather than as a separate one, and the *the* the ASV does write stands before the construct as a supplied one. Read the transliteration before counting: nothing is fronted from an article English has already spelled out. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amendments.why: Rule 29's attributive paragraph settles only one of the two orders an attributively rendered chain can take: the construct written as the attributive standing first. PRO.15 wrote the mirror order three times — `דְּבַר עֶצֶב` → *a grievous word* (15.1), `אִישׁ חֵמָה` → *A wrathful man* (15.18), `מַחְשְׁבוֹת רָע` → *Evil devices* (15.26) — where the rectum is the attributive and the construct is the English head noun. Two of those carry a supplied determiner, and both verses read it onto the construct, which is what this rule's own base sentence (*Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present*) directs. Left as it stood, the paragraph's counting sentence (*read which word each stands before*) invites the opposite reading in that order, since the determiner stands before the rectum's word; the same ambiguity is what produced this chapter's one patched verse in the order the rule does name. The added sentence states the outcome for the unnamed order and marks the boundary against rule 15's absolute-modifier case (`לֵב שָׂמֵחַ` → *A glad heart*, `שׁוֹר אָבוּס` → *a stalled ox*), which MACULA's morphology tells apart. It widens the existing rule where it stands rather than adding a cross-reference, and contradicts nothing in the corpus, which records no unit placing such a determiner on the rectum of an anarthrous chain.

conventions: Supplied determiner in an anarthrous construct chain: it belongs to the construct noun in both English orders. Where the construct is rendered attributively and stands first (`טוֹב־לֵב` → *a cheerful heart* 15.15, `מַרְפֵּא לָשׁוֹן` → *A gentle tongue* 15.4) and where the rectum is rendered attributively and the construct is the English head noun (`דְּבַר עֶצֶב` → *a grievous word* 15.1, `אִישׁ חֵמָה` → *A wrathful man* 15.18), the single written *a* or *the* is the construct noun's, and the rectum keeps only its own word together with whatever relational expression rule 19 gives it. The word standing next after the determiner is not what decides it. Rule 15's direction to take the noun of the expression governs a noun with an absolute modifier — `לֵב שָׂמֵחַ` → *A glad heart* (15.13), `כְּסִיל אָדָם` → *a foolish man* (15.20), `שׁוֹר אָבוּס` → *a stalled ox* (15.17) — where MACULA tags no construct, and read the morphology to tell the two apart.

The chapter's four ASV italics are disposed three ways, each by a named rule, and the table of candidates cannot show it because `added` units carry no source token. *doeth* (15.7) joins `זָרָה` as rule 34's pro-verb, because the Hebrew writes the verb it stands for in the first colon. *goeth* (15.24, 15.33) joins the fused directional `לְמַעְלָה` and the fused `לִפְנֵי` as the linking verb rule 49 puts on a prepositional or directional predicate, which rule 30 already licenses in naming `לִפְנֵי` → *was before*; the head stays on the word carrying the relation. *hath* (15.15) is `added`, because rule 43's count finds no `הָיָה`, no possessive preposition, no suffix and no verb of possession in that colon. *And* (15.10, 15.30) is `added`, because neither verse writes a conjunction morpheme at all. An italic corroborates and decides nothing in every one of these, by rule 7.

Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amended.why: Rule 29's attributive paragraph settles only one of the two orders an attributively rendered chain can take: the construct written as the attributive standing first. PRO.15 wrote the mirror order three times — `דְּבַר עֶצֶב` → *a grievous word* (15.1), `אִישׁ חֵמָה` → *A wrathful man* (15.18), `מַחְשְׁבוֹת רָע` → *Evil devices* (15.26) — where the rectum is the attributive and the construct is the English head noun. Two of those carry a supplied determiner, and both verses read it onto the construct, which is what this rule's own base sentence (*Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present*) directs. Left as it stood, the paragraph's counting sentence (*read which word each stands before*) invites the opposite reading in that order, since the determiner stands before the rectum's word; the same ambiguity is what produced this chapter's one patched verse in the order the rule does name. The added sentence states the outcome for the unnamed order and marks the boundary against rule 15's absolute-modifier case (`לֵב שָׂמֵחַ` → *A glad heart*, `שׁוֹר אָבוּס` → *a stalled ox*), which MACULA's morphology tells apart. It widens the existing rule where it stands rather than adding a cross-reference, and contradicts nothing in the corpus, which records no unit placing such a determiner on the rectum of an anarthrous chain.

report: One real cross-verse split: the supplied indefinite determiner of an anarthrous construct chain. PRO.15.4 (`מַרְפֵּא לָשׁוֹן` → *A gentle tongue*) gave it to the construct noun under rule 29's attributive paragraph; PRO.15.15 (`טוֹב־לֵב` → *of a cheerful heart*) gave the same word to the nomen rectum under rule 15. Same shape — construct rendered attributively standing before the rectum's own word, no article morpheme in the phrase, one written determiner — so 15.15 is patched to match. Only that verse is touched: t014 moves from `לֵב`'s unit into `טוֹב`'s.

The mirror order is already consistent and needs no patch: where the ASV renders the rectum attributively and the construct is the English head noun (`דְּבַר עֶצֶב` → *a grievous word* 15.1, `אִישׁ חֵמָה` → *A wrathful man* 15.18, `מַחְשְׁבוֹת רָע` → *Evil devices* 15.26), the determiner sits on the construct in every case. Rule 29 names only the other direction, so I amended it rather than let a later pass read its counting sentences as handing the word to the rectum.

The four ASV italics were checked as a set, since the candidate table is blind to `added` units. *doeth* (15.7) joins `זָרָה` as rule 34's pro-verb for a verb the coordination writes; *goeth* (15.24, 15.33) joins the fused directional and prepositional predicates as rule 49's linking verb, which rule 30 already licenses for `לִפְנֵי` → *was before*; *hath* (15.15) is `added` because rule 43's count finds no `הָיָה`, possessive preposition, suffix or verb of possession in that colon; *And* (15.10, 15.30) is `added` because no conjunction morpheme stands in either verse. Three dispositions, each by a named rule, no two verses of one shape treated differently. Recorded as a convention.

Checked and cleared as context-licensed, not splits: the eight rule 44 light-verb units all head on the complement with the competing head named (15.2, 15.5, 15.13, 15.14, 15.19, 15.20, 15.21, 15.30); the five supplied prepositions reaching a bare object all join the verb (15.3, 15.9, 15.14, 15.31, 15.32) and the sixth joins the predicate adjective under rule 33's valency paragraph (15.27); `בְּ` + suffix fuses to *therein*/*therewith* in all three places (15.4, 15.16, 15.17); `תּוֹעֲבַת יְהוָה` divides identically in 15.8, 15.9 and 15.26; every waw takes the connective the ASV wrote for it, and the *and*/*But*/*And* variation is read off the English as rule 14 directs.

BSB disagreements (3): PRO.15.12 `ל` and `וֹ`, where the ASV's passive *to be reproved* writes nothing for the dative and rule 40 marks both unrepresented; and PRO.15.17 `וְ`, where *where* is given to `שָׁם`, the morpheme whose own sense the word carries, under rule 11's priority, leaving the waw unrendered. Both are the documented convention difference — BSB attaches such morphemes to their phrase — and neither is a genuine error. Nothing was changed to improve the aggregate.
